# Conformance

`rimsky conformance` drives your service against the protocol's contract and prints one row per check. Install the `rimsky` binary from a release archive and point a subcommand at your endpoint.

```
rimsky conformance <subcommand> --endpoint <url> [flags]
```

Run `rimsky conformance` with no arguments, or with `help`, to print the subcommand list.

## The subcommands

Eight subcommands exist. Six drive a protocol; two drive something else.

| Subcommand | What it drives |
| --- | --- |
| `executor` | The `Executor` protocol, and `ExecutorObservability` under `--check-observability` |
| `claim-producer` | The `ClaimProducer` protocol, and `ClaimProducerObservability` under `--check-observability` |
| `publisher` | The `Publisher` protocol |
| `validation` | The `Validation` protocol |
| `data-processing` | The `DataProcessing` protocol |
| `lifecycle-subscriber` | The `LifecycleSubscriber` protocol |
| `blob-backend` | A blob backend, which is not a gRPC protocol |
| `probe` | The stub-mode probe on an executor, as a one-shot reachability check |

Two protocols have no subcommand of their own, and both are reachable through `--check-observability` on their sibling's subcommand: `ExecutorObservability` and `ClaimProducerObservability`.

One protocol has no conformance coverage at all. `HostAgent` has no subcommand, and `rimsky conformance host-agent` answers `unknown subcommand "host-agent"` with exit code 2. Test a host-agent implementation yourself.

## Shared flags

Every protocol subcommand takes `--endpoint` and `--timeout`. Most take `--transport`, which accepts `grpc` alone except on `claim-producer`, where it accepts `grpc` or `http`. `executor` and `lifecycle-subscriber` also take `--tls`, accepting `off` or `required`.

## Per-subcommand flags

**`executor`** — `--allow-live`, `--scenarios`, `--skip`, `--check-observability`, `--retention-test-seconds`, `--callback-bind`, `--callback-host`, `--tls`. The suite starts a callback receiver for async scenarios. Bind it on `0.0.0.0` and set `--callback-host` to a routable name when the executor runs in a container.

**`claim-producer`** — `--check-observability`, `--retention-test-seconds`. `--check-observability` requires `--transport grpc`; passing it with `--transport http` exits 2, because the kit has no HTTP+JSON path for `ClaimProducerObservability`.

**`publisher`** — `--kind` (required), `--resolved-config`, `--instance-id`, `--message-type`, `--control-api`. The message-push check runs only with both an instance id and a control-API URL, the latter from `--control-api` or `RIMSKY_CONTROL_API_URL`.

**`validation`** — `--role`, taking `executor`, `claim_producer`, `lifecycle_subscriber`, or `publisher`.

**`blob-backend`** — `--backend`, taking `memory`, `filesystem`, or `pg-largeobject`; `--root` for the filesystem backend; `--pg-conn-string` for the Postgres backend. It runs ten checks: two round-trips, a range read, an out-of-bounds range read, delete-then-read and delete-then-range-read, an empty payload, a non-empty self-describing handle, an idempotent delete, and concurrent writes.

**`probe`** — `--callback-bind`, `--callback-host`. It runs the stub-mode probe alone and reports whether the executor answered.

## Reading the result

Each check prints one line: `ok    <name>` or `FAIL  <name>: <error>`. A run with failures closes with `<subcommand>: N/M checks failed` on standard error.

Three exit codes exist:

| Code | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| 0 | Every check passed |
| 1 | Something went wrong at run time |
| 2 | Usage error |

Exit code 1 covers every run-time outcome: a failed check, a refused connection, an unopenable backend. A CI job reading the status alone cannot tell "your implementation failed a check" from "I never reached your endpoint". Parse the printed rows and the closing count to tell them apart.

No subcommand accepts `--json`; passing it exits 2 with `flag provided but not defined: -json`. None accepts `--warnings-as-errors` either.

## Running the executor suite

The executor suite refuses to start unless it can prove your executor is in stub mode, because its scenarios drive canned responses through probe attributes. Pass `--allow-live` to run against a live endpoint; stub-requiring scenarios then skip. When every scenario skips under `--allow-live`, the run reports that coverage was not verified and exits 0; when every scenario skips without it, the run exits 1.

Name scenarios to run with `--scenarios`, or scenarios to leave out with `--skip`, both comma-separated. A name neither list recognises fails the run before any scenario starts.

The nine scenarios are `execute_happy_path`, `attributes_serialization`, `malformed_attributes`, `park_emission`, `scratch_park_round_trip`, `tags_round_trip`, `async_handoff`, `async_callback_survives_restart`, and `cancel`.

## Running the suites from Go

Each suite is a package under `github.com/rimsky-ai/rimsky-core/lib/protocols/conformance`, so you can call it from your own test binary instead of shelling out. Every suite returns a slice of check results carrying a name and an error, which lets you fail your own test on the specific check you care about.
